vt36_guadalupe_tonantzin.topic: Guadalupe and Tonantzin: Tepeyac, the documents of the 1531 story, the authorship and historicity debates, the image

claims.text: Sahagún (1576, Book 11 appendix) wrote that at Tepeyac the Nahua had a temple to 'the mother of the gods, whom they called Tonantzin, which means Our Mother', with pilgrims from over twenty leagues; that preachers now called Our Lady 'Tonantzin'; that the proper title is 'Dios Inantzin'; and called it 'a satanic device to conceal idolatry'. He found the devotion 'suspicious' because pilgrims passed over other churches of Our Lady.

Tonantzin = to- 'our' + nān 'mother' + -tzin honorific; the title applied to several goddesses; Ruether (2005) doubts a single goddess named Tonantzin had a temple at Tepeyac and reads it as a maternal title
Apparition story: Juan Diego, 9-12 December 1531, Zumárraga, roses in the tilma; Zumárraga's extant writings do not mention it; feast 12 December

Miguel Sánchez, Imagen de la Virgen María 1648, first printed account, identified her with the Woman of the Apocalypse; Laso de la Vega published Huei tlamahuiçoltica 1649 (36 pp, mostly Nahuatl), containing the Nican Mopohua; Laso vicar of Tepeyac 1647-1657

Authorship: Sousa, Poole and Lockhart (1998) accept Laso as author drawing on Sánchez; León-Portilla and O'Gorman favour Antonio Valeriano c.1556; Sigüenza y Góngora's sworn statement named Valeriano; NYPL holds a partial copy dated to c.1556 (since 1880)

1556: Montúfar promoted the devotion; Bustamante's sermon of 8 September 1556 attacked it and said the image was painted by an Indian, Marcos (per the 1556 inquiry record, published 1888); Peterson supports Marcos Cipac de Aquino attribution; Poole and others sceptical
Poole, Our Lady of Guadalupe: Origins and Sources 1531-1797 (1995): no objective historical basis for the apparitions (Deck's summary); reviewers called it compelling
Schulenburg, abbot of the basilica, resigned 1996 after saying Juan Diego was a symbol not a reality; Codex Escalada announced 1995, dated 1548, contested; JPII beatified Juan Diego 6 May 1990

Juan Diego canonized 31 July 2002 at the Basilica by John Paul II, called first indigenous saint of the continent; homily presents Guadalupe as model of inculturated evangelization and speaks of the Virgin's mestizo face
Pius X decree Gratia quae 16 June 1910 patroness of Mexico; record 6.1 million pilgrims 11-12 Dec 2009; most-visited Catholic shrine
Nahua readings: blue-green mantle reserved for divine couple; belt as pregnancy; nahui ollin sign; rays as maguey spines (some)
López de Canseco: four-petal flower on belly = four cardinal points/four past eras; star positions said to match 12 Dec 1531 sky
Immaculate Conception/Woman of Revelation 12 iconography: sunburst, crescent moon underfoot, stars, hands joined

vt36_mothers_of_the_world.topic: Mothers of the world: Pachamama and Andean Virgins, the 2019 Tiber episode, Yemayá/Oshún and Iemanjá, Brigid, Black Madonnas

claims.text: Pachamama: Andean mother deity; through syncretism associated with the Virgin Mary, e.g. Virgin of Candelaria; challa libations, August offerings; JPII homilies in Peru 1985 and Bolivia 1988 described homage to Pachamama as recognising God's providence
Copacabana: image carved by Francisco Tito Yupanqui c.1576; adobe shrine c.1583; Augustinians from 1589; site of a former sun temple sacred to the Inca; basilica 2 July 1940

Virgin of the Mountain of Potosí, 1720, Museo Nacional de Arte La Paz: Virgin's body merges with the silver mountain; Trinity above, patrons below; some scholars read it as Pachamama syncretism; Spanish Virgin-mountain precedent (Montserrat)

Oct 2019: figures first shown at 4 Oct Vatican gardens tree-planting with Francis; displayed in Santa Maria in Traspontina; 21 Oct two men took them and threw them in Tiber; 25 Oct Francis: 'without idolatrous intentions', 'I ask forgiveness from those who have been offended'; recovered by Carabinieri; Ruffini: 'it represents life'
Alexander Tschugguel (Austria) claimed in a 4 Nov 2019 video he was one of the two; 'They do not belong in a Catholic church'
Our Lady of Charity: Benedict XV declared patroness of Cuba 10 May 1916 at request of independence veterans; crowned by JPII 24 Jan 1998; syncretized with Ochún

Yemoja: Yoruba water orisha (Ogun river); syncretized with Our Lady of Regla in Cuba, Our Lady of the Navigators/Conception in Brazil; syncretism emerged during slave trade; 2 Feb Rio Vermelho, 31 Dec beach offerings, 7 Sept Regla procession

Santería: roots in religions of enslaved West Africans in Cuba 16th-19th c.; Spanish colonial government permitted only Catholicism; two readings: concealment from authorities vs assimilation/social mobility; Lukumi v. Hialeah 1993

Brigid: c.451-525; Gerald of Wales (late 12th c.) on 19 nuns tending a fire at Kildare, men excluded; goddess Brigid shares name and attributes (Cormac's Glossary); scholars split between Christianised goddess and real woman absorbing traits; public holiday since 2023

Black Madonnas: c.400-500 in Europe; explanations: dark wood, soot, lead pigment ageing (Moss & Cappannari 1953), intentional (Begg), pre-Christian deity reinterpretation; research limited; Le Puy image destroyed in Revolution; Chartres 2014 restoration

vt36_isis_and_mary.topic: Isis and Mary: nursing images, Theotokos and Ephesus, Queen of Heaven and Star of the Sea, Wisdom, Mary Magdalene, Marian dogma, the approved-version thesis

claims.text: Isis lactans images c.700 BCE to 4th c. CE; Maria lactans in Egypt undisputed only from 7th c.; Higgins: similarity real but evidence does not justify deliberate cultic continuity
Isis lactans common in Ptolemaic period; scholars (e.g. Tran Tam Tinh 1973) explore possible links; continuity a possibility not established
Western Maria lactans: few before late Middle Ages; revived 12th c. with Cistercians; 100+ paintings first half of 13th c.; discouraged after Trent on grounds of propriety; Eastern Galaktotrophousa
Ephesus: 22 June-31 July 431, convened by Theodosius II, in the Church of Mary, Cyril presided, Nestorius deposed; Theotokos affirmed against Christotokos

Theotokos used before 431: Alexander of Alexandria c.321, Athanasius, Gregory Nazianzen; Sub tuum praesidium papyrus mostly dated after 450 (some say 3rd c.); article states it was originally a title of Isis (unsupported detail)

Artemision: Gothic raid 268; closed during late Roman persecution of pagans; Cyril credited John Chrysostom with destroying it, little evidence; Demeas inscription: 'Destroying the delusive image of the demon Artemis'; name erased from inscriptions
Queen of Heaven: Jeremiah 7:18 and 44:17-25 condemn cakes to the queen of heaven; Ephrem 4th c. calls Mary Lady and Queen; Regina Caeli 12th c.; Ad Caeli Reginam 11 Oct 1954; critics cite Jeremiah
Apuleius XI: Isis calls herself 'Queen of heaven, the principal of the Gods celestial', 'the natural mother of all things', named 'Queen Isis'; controls winds of the seas
Navigium Isidis 5 March, ship procession for seafarers; still celebrated in Italy at least until 416; suppressed in Egypt by Christian authorities in 6th c.
Stella Maris: Jerome's Liber de nominibus Hebraicis; probably originally 'stilla maris' (drop of the sea), copyist error; Isidore 7th c.; Ave Maris Stella c.8th c.; Paschasius Radbertus 9th c.

Sophia: Septuagint renders chokmah as sophia; Paul 1 Cor 1-2 Christ the wisdom of God; most Fathers identified Wisdom with Christ; Hagia Sophia 538 to Christ as Wisdom; icon 'Wisdom hath builded her house' shows Theotokos as house of Wisdom; Bulgakov's sophiology condemned by Russian Orthodox Church 1935
Munificentissimus Deus 1 Nov 1950: Mary 'was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory'; cites Pius IX's definition of the Immaculate Conception (Ineffabilis Deus)
JPII 22 Oct 1997 citing LG 66: Marian devotion 'differs essentially from the cult of adoration'; 'an infinite distance' from worship of Trinity
DDF Mater populi fidelis 4 Nov 2025 approved by Leo XIV 7 Oct: 'always inappropriate to use the title Co-redemptrix'; 'Christ is the only Mediator'

Gregory I to Mellitus 601: do not destroy temples but the idols in them; purify with holy water, place altars and relics; people 'come to places familiar and dear to them'; ox sacrifice replaced by 'some solemnity in exchange'
